subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-demo capacity & latency follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Sengupta <amit@fastretail.com>, Carla Martins <carla.m@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — quick recap + next steps

Hi Amit / Carla —

Great to meet you both on the demo. Short recap from our side and a proposed path so we can pick the right deployment mode for FastRetail.

Key signals from the call:
- Traffic shape: steady baseline ~1.5k requests/min (25 rps) for product recommendations, with microburst peaks reported during promo windows: up to 100k requests over a 10s window (10k rps).
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms for single-turn recommendation queries (median is less critical, p95 must be consistent).
- Payload: average prompt ~120 tokens, typical output ~40 tokens.
- Regulatory: no on-prem requirement today; possible VPC requirement for cardholder data later (scope TBD).

What this implies:
- Hosted API: easiest for time-to-value. Good if you accept brief tail latency variability during extreme microbursts or if you accept graceful degradation (fallback model / throttling).
- Dedicated capacity: recommended when you need predictable p95 under sustained or extreme microbursts — enables reserved GPU pools, predictable tail latency, and higher concurrency.

Proposed next steps (pick two):
1) Run a short synthetic microburst benchmark with your QPS profile (attach CSV) against Redwood hosted and dedicated test pools — 2 engineer-days, Redwood provides runbook and test harness.
2) If benchmarks favor Dedicated, we issue an SOW for a 30-day pilot (reserved pool + canary routing) and a one-week joint run to tune batching and KV caching.
3) If you want to start faster, we can launch Hosted with an automatic fallback to a smaller Dedicated pool for promotional windows (hybrid routing).

Action items:
- Amit: confirm which two options you'd like to run (benchmark + pilot OR benchmark + hosted-hybrid) and share any stricter latency SLOs you have.
- Marissa / PriyoM: I'll loop you on scheduling the benchmark and flag infra constraints.

Attaching your QPS profile you sent in the call notes.

Thanks —
Karthik

Looping in our test plan below (short):

Test plan summary:
- Two runs: (A) Hosted test against scale-out pool with synthetic replay; (B) Dedicated pilot simulation on 4x reserved GPUs.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tails during 10s microbursts, token/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and error/queueing rate.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 100ms for promo microburst windows, error rate <0.1%, no queue growth >5s.

We will provide the test harness (k6 + Redwood load driver) and a script to push your replay. Expected duration: 6–8 hours of run-time + 1 day to analyze.

If FastRetail confirms the two inputs Marissa listed, I'll provision the test pools and share an execution window.
